subject: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging and discount structure for Nebula Analytics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Blake <aaron@nebulaanalytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging and discount structure for Nebula Analytics

Hi Aaron —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I put together a short pilot outline that focuses on two things we heard from your team: 1) predictable unit economics for customer chat, and 2) minimizing latency while keeping per-token cost reasonable. Attachments include a short pilot scope and three commercial scenarios.

Quick summary of what we recommend evaluating during a 90-day pilot:
- Workload profile capture (we instrument a week of real traffic)
- KV/prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts (expected hit rate 25–45%)
- Two model variants: redwood-7b-quant-8 (default) and redwood-7b-quant-4 (eval-only)
- Autoscale and burst capacity for peak hours

Commercial framing options in the attachment (high level):
A) Commit credits (6-month reserve) + reduced per-token after cache & batching optimizations
B) Pay-as-you-go with stepped volume discount (3 tiers) + one-time onboarding credit
C) Hybrid: small commit + consumption overage at discounted rate + caching credits (to offset warm-up costs)

Technical notes in the deck: we expect caching to reduce billed tokens by ~20–35% for chat-heavy apps. Quantization to 8-bit is safe for production and offers immediate cost/throughput wins; 4-bit can give more savings but needs evals for hallucination/QA regressions.

Can you send a short note on anticipated monthly token volume (estimate range), primary latency SLO (p50/p95 targets), and whether this pilot needs to be on a VPC/private deployment due to data sensitivity? With those numbers I can model the three scenarios and propose a concession path that keeps us within margin while making a clear win for Nebula.

Attachment: optimize-toolkit-pilot-outline.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: pilot-cost-scenarios.csv (CSV)

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

From: Aaron Blake <aaron@nebulaanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-18T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging and discount structure for Nebula Analytics

Camila —

Thanks for this. A few data points up front:
- Expected starting volume: 0.8–1.2M tokens/month during pilot, with 3x growth if things go well.
- Traffic shape: very chatty (short interactions, median ~40 tokens) with occasional long reports (250–600 tokens).
- Latency target: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for 256-token responses.
- Data sensitivity: some user PII, but processed under our encrypted stream; we prefer a VPC/private deployment if the cost delta is manageable.

Question on quantization: we’ve seen mixed results; can you share a short benchmark or guideline for when 4-bit starts to show quality regressions vs 8-bit for instruction-following tasks? Also procurement will want a simple proposal (line items) they can plug into our PO — any way to give a clean single-sheet comparison of expected monthly spend under the three commercial frames?

I’ve CC’d our procurement alias (procure@nebulaanalytics.com) — they’ll be the ones to sign a PO.

— Aaron
Aaron Blake
CTO, Nebula Analytics
aaron@nebulaanalytics.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Blake <aaron@nebulaanalytics.com>, procure@nebulaanalytics.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-19T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: pilot packaging and discount structure for Nebula Analytics

Aaron —

Appreciate the detail. Attached is a one-page cost comparison that maps to your traffic profile (short chat plus occasional long responses). Highlights and recommendations:

- Baseline: redwood-7b-quant-8 + caching enabled. For 1M tokens/month with ~30% cache hit, estimated billed tokens ~700k. Estimated monthly spend (hosted): $5.8k (PAYG).
- Option A (6-month credit commit): 12% effective discount vs PAYG after caching/batching gains; includes $10k onboarding credit for integration/observability.
- Option B (PAYG with stepped tiers): 8% off at >1.5M tokens, 15% off >4M tokens.
- Option C (hybrid): small 3-month reserve that buys deeper short-term discounts plus explicit caching credits (covers warm-up cost of prefix cache).

Quantization guidance:
- 8-bit dynamic quantization: safe for instruction-following and retrieval-augmented generation; recommended as the production default.
- 4-bit (Q4_K/M modes): substantial CPU/GPU throughput gains and token-cost reduction (up to ~30–45% on model runtime), but we strongly recommend a small A/B eval set (50–200 prompts representative of your queries) to measure hallucination rate and instruction adherence before moving to production. We include a simple eval harness as part of the pilot.

Deployment mode: VPC/private increases baseline by ~25–35% vs hosted due to dedicated infra and networking. We can model that in the sheet — see column labeled 'VPC uplift'.

Attached: pilot-cost-scenarios.csv — contains the three commercial scenarios broken down by billed tokens, expected discounts, and example monthly spend. quant-recommendation.md has the quick benchmark plan for 4-bit vs 8-bit.

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement: confirm PO format and any necessary contract terms (I’ll draft a redline-ready SOW).
2) Tech: grant a short window (2–3 days) for our infra team to sample anonymized traffic or replay logs to tune cache params.
3) Commercial: confirm which scenario you want priced for legal/PO.

If procurement prefers a single-line monthly figure, we can give a conservative modeled spend with an itemized appendix.

Best,
Camila
Attachment: pilot-cost-scenarios.csv
Attachment: quant-recommendation.md
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: concession strategy for Nebula (DEAL-2025-089)

Camila / Lauren —

Quick internal note after reviewing the cost scenarios: margins are tight on pay-as-you-go for small pilots (high OSS and infra variability), so I recommend we prioritize a modest committed structure that still looks attractive. Suggested offer to Nebula:

- 6-month committed credits equivalent to $45k of usage (applied monthly), with a 15% effective discount across committed tokens after caching/batching adjustments.
- $15k one-time onboarding credit for integration and evals (covers our professional services and the eval harness).
- If Nebula signs an annual renewal within 90 days of pilot completion, convert remaining committed credits to a 12% ongoing spend rebate for first 12 months.

Rationale: this gives procurement a single PO item (commit + onboarding) while protecting our unit economics. Approvals required: Sales Director sign-off on >12% discount and CS Manager OK on $15k onboarding credit.

Camila — tbd: loop in Sales Director for final approval and flag margin impact. If we need to be more aggressive, we can add a one-time additional credit tied to adoption milestones (e.g., 50k monthly tokens after month 3).

— Aditya
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
